name: Hydrochloric Acid
description: A strong, corrosive acid commonly used in titrations and metal cleaning.
properties: Colorless to pale yellow liquid; pungent odor; highly soluble in water.
safety_notes: Corrosive. Causes severe skin burns and eye damage. Use gloves and goggles.

name: Sodium Hydroxide
description: A strong base widely used in titrations, saponification, and pH adjustment.
properties: White solid or solution; highly soluble in water; exothermic on dissolving.
safety_notes: Corrosive. Causes severe skin burns and eye damage.

name: Silver Nitrate
description: Used to test for halide ions via precipitation reactions.
properties: Colorless crystalline solid; soluble in water; light-sensitive.
safety_notes: Oxidizer. Stains skin and clothing. Avoid contact with light and organic matter.

name: Sodium Chloride
description: Common table salt, frequently used as a source of chloride ions.
properties: White crystalline solid; freely soluble in water.
safety_notes: Low hazard. Avoid ingestion of laboratory-grade material.

name: Copper(II) Sulfate
description: A blue salt used in displacement reactions and electroplating demonstrations.
properties: Blue crystalline solid; soluble in water forming a blue solution.
safety_notes: Harmful if swallowed. Irritant to skin and eyes.

name: Zinc
description: A reactive metal used to demonstrate single displacement reactions.
properties: Bluish-grey solid metal; reacts with acids releasing hydrogen gas.
safety_notes: Flammable as powder/dust. Bulk metal is low hazard.

name: Sulfuric Acid
description: A strong dibasic acid used in neutralization and dehydration reactions.
properties: Colorless, oily, highly corrosive liquid; strongly exothermic with water.
safety_notes: Highly corrosive. Always add acid to water, never the reverse.

name: Sodium Carbonate
description: A mild base used to demonstrate acid-carbonate reactions releasing CO2.
properties: White solid; soluble in water forming a mildly alkaline solution.
safety_notes: Irritant to eyes and skin in concentrated form.

name: Barium Chloride
description: Used to test for sulfate ions via precipitation.
properties: White crystalline solid; soluble in water.
safety_notes: Toxic if ingested. Handle with gloves.

name: Potassium Iodide
description: A source of iodide ions used in precipitation and redox demonstrations.
properties: White crystalline solid; soluble in water.
safety_notes: Low hazard. Avoid prolonged skin contact.

name: Lead(II) Nitrate
description: Used to demonstrate double displacement reactions producing lead halide precipitates.
properties: White crystalline solid; soluble in water.
safety_notes: Toxic. Contains lead; avoid ingestion and skin contact.

name: Magnesium
description: A reactive metal that burns brightly and reacts readily with dilute acids.
properties: Silvery-white solid metal; ribbon or powder form.
safety_notes: Flammable, especially as powder/ribbon. Do not look directly at burning magnesium.
